name: Customers
description: Records, entities, wallets, parent and child billing.
takeaways: Name is the only required field
Business entity is fixed after creation
Child invoices go to the parent, not merged

cards.title: Core fields
cards.body: Name is the only required field. External ID and email must each be unique in the organization, so they work as lookup keys for matching external systems.
cards.example: Acme Corp, external ID acme-001, billing@acme.com.

cards.title: Business entity
cards.body: Each customer belongs to one business entity, the legal entity that issues its invoices. The dashboard does not let you change it after creation.
cards.example: A German and a US entity exist; Acme is created under the German one.

cards.title: Addresses and tax IDs
cards.body: The billing address appears on invoices; shipping defaults to billing. The tax ID type follows the country (GST, VAT, TIN).
cards.example: Pick Germany and the VAT field appears.

cards.title: Contacts
cards.body: Any number of extra people, each independently set to receive invoice communications.
cards.example: finance@acme.com gets invoices; the CTO does not.

cards.title: Wallet
cards.body: A per-currency credit balance applied when an invoice is approved, unless turned off for that invoice. Earlier contract experience only.
cards.example: A $200 promo credit reduces a $1,000 invoice to $800.

cards.title: Parent and child
cards.body: A child customer still generates its own invoice, but it is billed to and paid by the parent. Nothing is merged. Earlier contract experience only.
cards.example: Three subsidiaries each get an invoice, all addressed to headquarters.

cards.title: Consolidated invoice
cards.body: Separately, you can manually combine already-generated invoices of linked customers into one document from the invoice list.
cards.example: Merge the three subsidiary invoices at month end.

cards.title: Customer portal
cards.body: A self-service view where customers see their invoice details. A session for a customer or guest can be created through the API.
cards.example: Create a session so a customer can view their invoices.

cards.title: Account-level fields
cards.body: Defined once in Settings, then shown on every customer: transaction type, tier, segment. A required one must be filled before saving.

cards.title: Tax exemption
cards.body: There is no standard tax-exempt field. It appears only if you define an exempt tax custom attribute for customers.
cards.example: Add an Exempt checkbox attribute, then mark charities as exempt.

edgeCases: Unique keys. External ID and email must each be unique in the organization.
Business entity. It cannot be changed in the dashboard after creation. This is enforced in the edit form, not on the record itself.
Deleting. A customer cannot be deleted while any contract references it. Remove it from every contract first. Deletion is a soft delete.
Newer contract experience. Wallets and the Add as child toggle are not shown under Contracts V3.
Tax exemption. Needs a custom attribute you define yourself.
Contact settings. The contract-communications setting exists in the data model but has no dashboard control today.

quiz.question: What is the only required field on a customer?
quiz.explanation: Name is required; external ID and email must be unique when present.

quiz.question: Can you delete a customer that a contract still references?
options: Yes, the contract is deleted too
No, remove it from every contract first
quiz.explanation: Deletion is blocked while a contract references the customer, and it is a soft delete.

quiz.question: A child customer generates usage. Who pays the invoice?
options: The parent, on the child's own separate invoice
quiz.explanation: The child keeps its own invoice, addressed to and paid by the parent.

quiz.question: Where does a tax-exempt flag come from?
quiz.explanation: It appears only if the organization defines an exempt tax custom attribute.

quiz.question: When are wallet credits applied?
options: At invoice approval, unless turned off for that invoice
quiz.explanation: Credits offset the amount due when the invoice is approved.

qa.question: Customer vs contact?
qa.answer: The customer is the entity you bill. Contacts are extra people on it, each with their own invoice-communication setting.

qa.question: External ID vs Zenskar ID?
qa.answer: The Zenskar ID is the internal identifier. The external ID is your own identifier. Send a UUID and Zenskar can use it as the ID; send a non-UUID and it is stored as the external ID.

qa.question: Wallet vs credit note?
qa.answer: A wallet is a per-currency credit balance applied when an invoice is approved. A credit note is created against a specific invoice.

qa.question: Parent and child billing vs consolidated invoices?
qa.answer: Parent and child routes a child's own invoice to the parent for payment. Consolidation manually combines already-generated invoices of linked customers into one document.

qa.question: Customer vs business entity?
qa.answer: The business entity is your legal entity that issues invoices. The customer is who you bill, and belongs to one entity.

qa.question: custom_data vs custom_attributes?
qa.answer: They are the same idea under different API names: the Customer object uses custom_data, while contracts and products use custom_attributes. A separate field also named custom_attributes on some objects is for tagging.

qa.question: Billing address vs shipping address?
qa.answer: Billing appears on invoices and drives regional tax calculation. Shipping defaults to billing.

qa.question: auto_charge_enabled vs communications_enabled?
qa.answer: Auto charge controls automatic payment charging. Communications controls emails such as invoices and receipts.

qa.question: Link a customer to Stripe?
qa.answer: Set the connector with name stripe and the Stripe customer ID as reference_id, through the customer connector endpoint or the bulk import.

qa.question: Migrate customers from a CRM?
qa.answer: Send the CRM ID as external_id so you can match records both ways.

qa.question: Subsidiaries paying through headquarters?
qa.answer: Use parent and child billing: each child still gets an invoice, billed to the parent.

qa.question: Give a customer a promotional balance?
qa.answer: A wallet credit reduces the next approved invoice.

qa.question: Mark a charity tax exempt?
qa.answer: Define an exempt tax custom attribute for customers, then set it on the charity.

qa.question: Send invoices only to finance?
qa.answer: Add the finance address as a contact with invoice communications on, and leave it off for other contacts.

qa.question: Can I delete a customer with contracts?
qa.answer: No. Remove it from every contract first. Deletion is a soft delete.

qa.question: What if two customers share an email?
qa.answer: Email must be unique in the organization, so the second create fails.

qa.question: Can a customer change business entity?
qa.answer: Not in the dashboard after creation.

qa.question: What if the address is missing or wrong?
qa.answer: Regional tax calculation depends on it, so tax can be wrong or unresolved.

qa.question: Why was a customer not pushed to Stripe?
qa.answer: Export only pushes a customer when it is first created. Existing customers need the bulk CSV import with a reference_id column.

qa.question: Where are wallets under Contracts V3?
qa.answer: Wallets and the Add as child toggle are not shown under the newer experience.

qa.question: How does usage find its customer?
qa.answer: A usage event carries customer_id, which a metric matches to external ID or Zenskar ID by default.

qa.question: How do I enable consolidated invoices through the API?
qa.answer: Older reference docs describe setting parent_customer_id and invoice_consolidation_enabled in custom_data.
